title: VibeGraph IR
description:
Intermediate representation emitted by scripts/parse_cst.py for a single Python source file. Pins the existing { version, nodes, edges, symbolIndex } shape and per-construct discriminated fields. See PLAN.md §1.1.

v1.1 adds optional `modulePath` on root + optional `targetFile` and `qualifiedTarget` on edges (cross-file references, emitted by scripts/cross_file_link.py in project mode) + optional `callTarget` on assignment nodes.

v1.2 (M8.2 — pulled forward from M9.1) adds optional `decorators: string[]` on FunctionDefNode and ClassDefNode (decorator source text, used by discover_entry_points.py for Flask/FastAPI route detection and M9's semantic icon system).

v1.3 (M9.1) adds optional `effectKind` enum (db|http|fs|subprocess|log) on CallNode + AssignmentNode (when valueKind=='call') for the M9 icon system + thread external-effects panel, and `isAsync` boolean on FunctionDefNode (always present) for the async function variant.

v1.4 (M17.1) adds optional `viaLocal` on reference edges — set when a method call's receiver is a local variable rather than an imported module (e.g. `parser.add_subparsers()` where `parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(...)` three lines up). The edge's `target` then points at the receiver's assignment node (same file); `qualifiedTarget` carries the fully resolved external/project symbol (e.g. `argparse:ArgumentParser.add_subparsers`); `viaLocal` records the receiver name for display.

v1.5 (M17.2) extends the `NodeType` enum with four control-flow container kinds — `try_stmt`, `except_handler`, `finally_block`, `while_loop` — so the thread renderer can group call sites by their enclosing control-flow construct. Statements inside a `try` / `except` / `finally` / `while` arm have their `parentId` pointing at the container, not the enclosing function. This is a non-additive enum extension: consumers that switch on `node.type` may encounter unknown values. Per-arm shape: try_stmt has no extras; except_handler carries `exceptType: string | null`; finally_block has no extras; while_loop carries `condition: string` (mirroring IfStmt). All v1.0 → v1.4 IRs still validate. v1.5 IRs validate as long as consumers tolerate the four new enum members.

Additions through v1.4 are field-additive and backwards-compatible — v1.0 / v1.1 / v1.2 / v1.3 IRs still validate. v1.5 is enum-additive: structurally backwards-compatible (no required field changes), but consumers must accept the four new NodeType values to render M17.2 IRs.

v2.0 (M-LANG1, PLAN-M-LANG.md) is the MAJOR bump for multi-language frontends: a `language` discriminator (python|bash|jsts|cpp), REQUIRED when version=='2.0', optional (server-stamped, like `filePath`) on earlier versions. At 2.0 the Python-flavoured fields — `decorators`, `isAsync`, `returns` semantics, `docstring`, `annotation`, the `fstring` ValueKind, the `'x as y'` import-name convention, dotted `modulePath` — are LANGUAGE-OPTIONAL: a frontend emits them only where its language has the concept (absence is honest, never faked). `modulePath` is generalised to a language-defined module identity (Python: dotted path; other languages may use project-relative file paths). The NodeId grammar is unchanged. parse_cst.py continues to emit 1.5; only new-language frontends emit 2.0. All v1.x IRs still validate.

M-CMD.1 adds optional `degraded` on the root: a partial parse now says so IN the IR. Field-additive; every prior IR still validates.

version.description: IR schema version. v1.0 = M1 baseline; v1.1 = M4a (cross-file refs); v1.2 = M8.2 (decorators on FunctionDef/ClassDef); v1.3 = M9.1 (effectKind on call/assignment, isAsync on FunctionDef); v1.4 = M17.1 (viaLocal on reference edges for local-variable receivers); v1.5 = M17.2 (control-flow container nodes: try_stmt, except_handler, finally_block, while_loop — parentId-shifts children inside their arms); v2.0 = M-LANG1 (multi-language major: `language` discriminator required, Python-flavoured fields become language-optional).

language.description: Source-language discriminator (M-LANG1). REQUIRED when version=='2.0' (emitted by the language frontend); on v1.x IRs it is optional and stamped by the server (like `filePath`) — absence means python.

modulePath.description: Language-defined module identity relative to project root. Python: dotted path (e.g. 'main', 'pkg.sub.mod' — __init__.py collapses to the package name). Other language frontends may use project-relative file paths (e.g. 'lib/common.sh'). Present only in project mode; absent in single-file mode.

filePath.description: Optional source path attached by the server when emitting an AstPayload. Not produced by the bare parser.

degraded.description: M-CMD.1 — present ONLY when the frontend could not read part of this file and dropped it. The IR is still emitted (a partial map beats no map) but it is INCOMPLETE, and a consumer must be able to learn that from the IR itself rather than from a separate error map it may never see. Absence means nothing was dropped. Field-additive; emitted by the four tree-sitter frontends, which count ERROR and MISSING nodes as they walk. libcst either parses a file or raises, so Python emits no IR at all for a file it cannot read and never carries this field.

dropped.description: How many constructs the parser could not read.

note.description: The sentence a human or a model reads.

NodeId.description: Structural-path ID. Always starts with 'module'. Subsequent segments are either '<name>.<kind>' (import|import_from|assign|fn|class|call) or '<kind>@<n>' for nameless statements (for|if|return|raise|call|try|except|finally|while). Slashes separate parents from children. Never contains line numbers.

Position.description: Source range. Lines are 1-indexed; columns are 0-indexed. parse_cst.py always emits numeric values for every field.

NodeType.description: Closed enum of structural node kinds emitted by parse_cst.py. Adding a kind is a schema change. v1.5 (M17.2) added try_stmt / except_handler / finally_block / while_loop as control-flow container kinds — statements inside their arms have `parentId` pointing at the container, not the enclosing function. M-COMP added `comprehension`, a fifth container kind on the same terms: a comprehension IS a loop, and without a container the N+1 verdict depended on whether the author wrote `[f(x) for x in xs]` or the spelled-out for-loop. A file emitting it stamps version 1.5, like the other containers. M-SKILLS.3 added `interface_def` (JS/TS only, so a file emitting it already stamps 2.0): a node is also the ADDRESS an edit is sent to, and a TypeScript `interface` had none — a work-run packet escalated with "the interface declaration is unreachable through the CST edit", failed, and cost its arm the task, while `src/` alone held 374 equally unreachable interfaces. It carries no thread value and the extractor never walks it. Type aliases (`type X = …`) are the same class and deliberately NOT emitted yet — 100 in `src/`, none in any fixture, and not the measured failure.

EdgeType.description: Closed enum of edge kinds. 'contains' is emitted automatically by _emit() for parent-child relationships; 'reference' is emitted at call sites and inheritance; 'data' is emitted on iterable->for_loop flow; 'control' is reserved for branch flow (not currently emitted but reserved by protocol.ts).

EffectKind.description: v1.3+: classifies an external-system call. String-match heuristic per PLAN-v2.md §2.1; false positives expected (the icon system is for scanning, not correctness claims).

NestsInnerCalls.description:
M-NEST (field-additive, no version bump): true when this statement's expression hides at least one call beyond its outermost call — arg-nests, method chains, literal-embedded calls. This is the honesty signal the view badges. Absent (treated as false) when the expression has no nested call.

M-COMP: calls inside a COMPREHENSION are NO LONGER counted. They used to be a hiding place; they now sit as real call nodes inside a `comprehension` container, so counting them would badge the outer step 'path shown incomplete' about calls the reader can see. A list LITERAL still counts — `f([g(x), h(y)])` genuinely hides two calls behind one step.

NestExtracted.description:
M-NEST (field-additive, no version bump): present only alongside nestsInnerCalls. true when v1 actually minted child `call` nodes (the nesting was inside call ARGUMENTS); false when the nesting was detected but deferred (chains/literals) — those are honestly badged but not yet decomposed into nodes. This false case IS the documented stopping rule.

M-COMP removed comprehensions from that list: they are not deferred any more, they are decomposed into a `comprehension` container, so they no longer set nestsInnerCalls at all and never reach this field.

ValueKind.description: Discriminator for assignment value shape. Maps to libcst expression types in _value_kind().

SymbolKind.description: Closed enum of symbol kinds. 'method' is reserved for future class-aware emission; current parser uses 'function' for both module-level and class-level defs. 'interface' (M-SKILLS.3) is emitted by the JS/TS frontend beside its interface_def node, so a TypeScript type is findable by name as well as addressable by id.

BaseNode.description: Common fields on every node. Per-type extras are pinned by the discriminated union in Node.

parentId.description: Parent node ID, or null at module scope.

ImportNode.description: `import x` / `import x as y`. Aliases are encoded in-string as 'x as y'.

ImportFromNode.description: `from x.y import a, b`. `module` is empty string for relative-only imports (`from . import …`).

AssignmentNode.description: Single-target assignment. Multi-target tuple-destructure currently records only the first target. `name` may be dotted (e.g. 'self.name'); `preview` is truncated source. `callTarget` is present iff valueKind=='call' (v1.1+) and is the dotted callee name — used by cross_file_link.py to resolve assignment-RHS calls. `effectKind` (v1.3+) classifies the call's external-system effect when valueKind=='call'. `annotation` (field-additive, no version bump) carries the type-annotation source text for annotated assignments (`x: int`, dataclass fields); the declaration-only form (`uid: int`, no RHS) has an empty `preview` and `valueKind='other'`. `args` / `kwargs` (field-additive, no version bump) carry the structured constructor arguments when valueKind=='call' — positional arg source strings and {name,value} keyword pairs, full (untruncated, unlike `preview`). Star-args (`*x`/`**y`) are omitted from both. Used by the architecture view to read individual layer args (e.g. nn.Conv2d(3,64,3) → args ['3','64','3']) and compute per-layer param counts from literal values.

augmented.description: M-ORCH.3 (2026-09-07, field-additive, no version bump): present iff the statement is an AUGMENTED assignment (`x += f()`), carrying the operator source text ("+=", "-=", …). Before this, libcst's AugAssign emitted nothing, so a call on its right-hand side was invisible to the linker and the thread extractor. Such a node never DEFINES its name (the target already exists) — it carries the call, the effect, the args, and the reference edge like any assignment.

FunctionDefNode.description: `def name(...)`. Methods are emitted with type='function_def' too — distinguish via parentId pointing at a class_def. `docstring` is null when absent (always present as a key). `decorators` (v1.2+) is the source-text list of decorator expressions, e.g. ['app.route("/")', 'login_required']; empty array when bare. `isAsync` (v1.3+) is true for `async def`, false for sync; always present. `returns` (§5.5, field-additive, no version bump — mirrors `annotation` on AssignmentNode) is the return-type annotation source text (the expression after `->`, e.g. 'sqlite3.Connection'), or null when unannotated; consumed by cross_file_link.py for one-hop return-type inference of lowercase-bound receivers (`conn = _get_conn()` where `_get_conn` is annotated → `conn.execute` resolves to honest-external `sqlite3.Connection.execute` instead of `dynamic`).

decoratorLine.description: M-CONTRACT.6 (2026-09-08, field-additive, no version bump): the 1-based line of the FIRST decorator when the def is decorated; absent otherwise. `line` keeps libcst's span start (the `def` keyword) for every consumer keyed on it; line-slicing readers (get_node_source, the node editor) start at `decoratorLine ?? line` so what a caller reads is exactly the decorated node that replace_node replaces.

paramTypes.description: M-CONTRACT (2026-09-07, field-additive, no version bump — the `returns` precedent): {param name → annotation source text} for every ANNOTATED parameter (`limit: int` → {"limit": "int"}); absent when no parameter is annotated. `params` keeps its `name` / `name=default` strings untouched so every consumer keyed on it is unchanged; the thread contract renders `name: type` from this map. Non-Python frontends already carry the type inside `params` (`limit: number`, `const Item& item`) and do not emit this field.

ClassDefNode.description: `class Name(Base, ...)`. `bases` is always present (empty array if no bases). `decorators` (v1.2+) is the source-text list of decorator expressions, empty when bare. `docstring` (M-FS6, field-additive, no version bump — mirrors function_def) is the class docstring or null; consumed by entry-point discovery so class entries carry a summary like function entries do.

decoratorLine.description: M-CONTRACT.6 — see FunctionDefNode.decoratorLine: where a decorated class (@dataclass) really starts.

InterfaceDefNode.description: A TypeScript `interface` declaration (JS/TS frontend only; a file emitting it already stamps 2.0). It carries NO thread value — an interface calls nothing and the extractor never walks it — and exists because a node is also the ADDRESS an edit is sent to: the chokepoint targets IR ids, so a construct without one cannot be changed at all. M-SKILLS.3 measured the cost: a work-run packet escalated with "the interface declaration is unreachable through the CST edit", failed, and cost its arm the task. `isExported` / `isDefaultExport` mirror FunctionDefNode (M-CMD.1). Type aliases (`type X = ...`) are the same class and deliberately not emitted yet.

ForLoopNode.description: `for target in iter:`. `iterName` is the source text of the iterable expression.

iterSep.description: How the SOURCE spells the separator in a for-each header, when the language has more than one and the frontend can read it: JS `for…in` walks keys and `for…of` walks values, and a label that picks one for the other names a different construct. Absent = the language has a single spelling and the reader uses its default (Python/bash `in`, C++ `:`).

IfStmtNode.description: `if cond:` with optional else/elif arm. `condition` is the source text of the test. `elseLine` (M17.3, field-additive — no version bump, mirrors the v1.1–v1.4 additive convention) is present whenever the if has a trailing arm (`hasElse: true`); it's the start line of that arm (the `else:` block, or the nested `elif` If). The thread extractor uses it to split call sites into if_then (line < elseLine) vs if_else (line >= elseLine) containers. For `elif`, the nested If sits in the outer if's else arm, so a call reached through it lands in if_else and the elif's own if_stmt nests inside that else container.

ReturnStmtNode.description: `return [value]`. `value` is the truncated source of the returned expression, or null for bare `return`. M-NEST: when the returned expression is a direct call (`return self.fc(x)`), `callTarget` carries the dotted callee (so the architecture forwardSeq surfaces the layer it applies) and `effectKind` classifies any external effect. `nestsInnerCalls`/`nestExtracted` flag nested calls inside the returned expression.

RaiseStmtNode.description: `raise [exc]`. `exc` is the truncated source of the raised expression, or null for bare `raise`. M-NEST: when the raised expression is a direct call (`raise ValueError(msg)`), `callTarget`/`effectKind` mirror the return_stmt fields; `nestsInnerCalls`/`nestExtracted` flag nested calls in the raised expression.

CallNode.description: Bare expression-statement call (e.g. `print(x)`) OR (M-NEST) a call nested inside another call's arguments. Top-level statement calls carry just funcName/args/isEffect. Nested calls (minted by the M-NEST arg-walk) additionally carry `nested: true`, `nestedDepth` (1 for a direct arg-nest, higher for multi-level), `callTarget` (mirrors funcName so the architecture forwardSeq surfaces nested layer applications), and a `preview`. Their parentId points at the enclosing call/assignment/return node, with a `contains` edge wiring outer→inner. `effectKind` (v1.3+) classifies the external-system effect when the funcName matches one of the §2.1 detection rules.

TryStmtNode.description: v1.5 (M17.2): `try:` container. Statements directly inside the try body have parentId pointing at this node. The matching `except_handler` / `finally_block` nodes are emitted as siblings (parented at the same scope as the try_stmt), not children — keeping the IR's parent chain a clean structural tree without arm-specific traversal logic. The relationship between `try_stmt` and its arms is positional (line proximity in source order).

ExceptHandlerNode.description: v1.5 (M17.2): `except [Type [as name]]:` arm of a try. `exceptType` is the source text of the caught exception (e.g. 'ValueError', 'Exception'), or null for bare `except:`. Statements inside the handler have parentId pointing at this node.

FinallyBlockNode.description: v1.5 (M17.2): `finally:` arm of a try. Statements inside the finally have parentId pointing at this node.

WhileLoopNode.description: v1.5 (M17.2): `while cond:` container. `condition` is the source text of the test (mirrors IfStmt). Statements inside the loop body have parentId pointing at this node.

ComprehensionNode.description:
M-COMP: a list / set / dict comprehension or generator expression, as a LOOP CONTAINER. `compKind` is list|set|dict|generator; `target` and `iterName` mirror ForLoopNode.

ONE NODE PER `for` CLAUSE, nested outermost-first. A comprehension may carry several clauses, and they are NESTED LOOPS: `[f(x) for g in groups for x in g]` runs f exactly as often as the spelled-out `for g: for x: f(x)`, and emits the same two-deep container shape. `target`/`iterName` carry THAT clause's source text, not the whole comprehension's.

Parenting follows evaluation order, not source order. The outermost iterable is evaluated ONCE before any element is produced, so calls in it parent OUTSIDE this node — the same rule ForLoopNode applies to `for x in fetch_all():`. Everything that repeats parents INSIDE: the element expression, every `if` clause, and every INNER `for` clause's iterable.

A comprehension reached through an expression that itself runs in the enclosing flow (a `for` iterable, an `if` test) parents at that enclosing scope, NOT inside the construct's container — `for x in [f(y) for y in ys]` builds the list once, before the loop starts.

Generator expressions get a container like the eager three. They are lazy, so the repetition is only real once something consumes them, and whether that happens is NOT tracked — a named limit. The alternative was worse: the effect floor already emits the element's call node for a genexp, so excluding the container would have made the round-trip verdict depend on bracket choice while the effect verdict did not.

Node.description: Discriminated union over node types. The `type` field selects which extra fields are required.

Edge.description: Directed edge between two node IDs. `contains` is auto-emitted by _emit(); other kinds are emitted by specific visitors. v1.1+: edges may carry `targetFile` (absolute path) and `qualifiedTarget` (e.g. 'models:User') when the edge crosses files — `target` then refers to a NodeId inside the foreign file's IR. v1.4+: edges may carry `viaLocal` (the receiver-variable name) for reference edges where the call's receiver is a local variable bound to an external class — `target` points at the receiver's assignment node (same file), `qualifiedTarget` resolves through the binding to the external symbol.

targetFile.description: Absolute path of the file containing the target node. Absent for intra-file edges.

qualifiedTarget.description: Qualified symbol path of the target (e.g. 'models:User', 'pkg.sub.mod:fn'). Display/debugging hint; resolution is via {targetFile, target}.

viaLocal.description: v1.4+: name of the local variable through which this edge resolves. Present when a call like `parser.add_subparsers()` was resolved via `parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(...)` — `target` then points at the assignment node, `qualifiedTarget` at the resolved method (e.g. `argparse:ArgumentParser.add_subparsers`).

viaReturnType.description: §5.5 (field-additive, no version bump): true ONLY when a viaLocal edge resolved through one-hop return-type inference — the receiver was bound from a function call whose return annotation named the type (`conn = _get_conn()` where `def _get_conn() -> sqlite3.Connection:`), NOT a direct class instantiation. The run-to-node effect scan (scan_effects.py) reads this to refuse conservatively: the external method's purity is unprovable and the parse-time effectKind heuristic (receiver-name based) can miss non-conventional names.

SymbolLoc.description: Symbol location. Matches Position but `endCol` is nullable per protocol.ts:SymbolEntry — kept for forward compatibility even though the current parser always emits a number.

Symbol.description: Entry in symbolIndex. Pinned by protocol.ts:SymbolEntry. `sym` is a stable key like 'function:foo' / 'class:Bar'; `scope` is either 'module' or a parent node ID.

scope.description: 'module' for top-level symbols, otherwise a NodeId (e.g. 'module/Shape.class' for a method).
